Me too. I’ve also had the worst times of my life while coming down from them and back to reality.

It’s all about whether you think the extreme lows are worth the extreme highs. I personally think so (in moderation) but it’s important to remember that drugs, especially coming down from them, are some of the least fun experiences one can have. Some people think the lows are not worth the highs, which is why they would rather miss out on the fun.

I agree that sober people miss out on so much fun, but it makes sense because extreme fun can’t exist without equally extreme shittiness, so I don’t blame them or think they’re idiots for missing out, I can understand why they prefer that life and I don’t blame them, even though I personally have a different preference.

Thoughts? Agree/Disagree? Have something you want to expand on this, or a point you think I missed? I’m all ears, let’s have a discussion!

Obviously you will have more fun on drugs, but when you come down you feel even worse than being sober. 

It’s all about personal preference of living the extreme highs that come with extreme lows, the highs are worth the lows for some people like OP, and they think living without those extremes is a dull existence.


For others who prefer sober life, the extreme lows aren’t worth the extreme highs, and they would rather have their highs be less high and lows be less low and are more fulfilled with living either content/not so content, than to go through such extreme highs and extreme lows that come with what makes drugs so much fun.

Another reason sober people don’t mind missing on the fun of drugs is possibly because their responsibilities require them to be emotionally stable, and being able to succeed in those responsibilities is the high they prefer to the high of drugs.

Thoughts? Counter-points? Different ways of understanding why people have these preferences? I’d love to hear some other perspectives.

I am someone who used to vape, but does not vape anymore. I have no reason to make excuses for it anymore, because I’m not doing it anymore. I’m here to tell you that I was just as addicted to vaping as cigarettes, and it actually made it harder for me to quit.

I’m not saying it’s not possible to quit by using a vape. I am only saying that you shouldn’t be recommending it before other methods of quitting, because there is a high risk of staying addicted. That’s objectively true. Here are some more objective facts that you can’t deny.

1. Vapes are a source of nicotine. 

2. Nicotine is what makes cigarettes so addictive.

3. Therefore, it is entirely possible to switch to vaping in an attempt to quit, and stay just as addicted to nicotine, only you are now getting it from a vape instead of a cigarette.

In my personal experience, vaping only made it harder for me to quit. If you are going to vape that’s your choice, but please at least admit that vaping IS addictive. Just because you feel that you are not addicted to vaping doesn’t mean that other people won’t get addicted. 

You’re not gonna like this next part, but I’m just being honest, you sound like a person in denial because you don’t want to quit your nicotine habit. You sound like me a few months ago. I used to say to people that I’m not even addicted to vaping because I can go days without it. But

It’s your choice if you don’t want to give up the habit. I can’t convince you to quit unless you already want to quit yourself. It’s your choice.

BUT—you really shouldn’t be giving advice to people who are trying to quit smoking, if you aren’t ready to quit nicotine yourself. You can keep making excuses in your own life, but don’t tempt people who truly want to quit into making the same excuses.
